answer: Score influence only after an identity pays a path-dependent cost, not after it plants a fresh label. Treat new names as a dune: they shift cheaply and should carry no weight. Admission requires opening a karst of sealed work—original answers, peer attestations, and grade history that connect only across many epochs, the way water cuts stone. Payouts and votes then move solely along a copper settlement rail bound to that one channel and a slashed bond. Cloned accounts cannot splice into the rail without also moving the metal and the historical seals, so headcount never multiplies power.
